sections.h2: Which side of the state line is the house on?
sections.html:
That question comes first in Texarkana, because the city is two municipalities. A house on the Texas side sits in Bowie County and follows Texas law, while one across State Line Avenue in Arkansas follows Arkansas rules and is recorded in Miller County. This page covers the Texas side.

If yours is a Texas address, a quick sale can take three common forms. Each fits a different situation, and the sections below explain the local pieces that touch all of them.

  • Cash purchase: the buyer pays without a mortgage and can close when your title work is clear.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, with inspections and lender timelines.
  • Sale subject to repairs: the buyer credits you or asks for fixes after an inspection.

sections.h2: How did the Texas half of Texarkana come about?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas says the town was established on December 8, 1873, where the Texas and Pacific Railway met the line from Arkansas, and that the Texas railroad laid out its side of the plat from the rail yards to Seventh Street. The Texas city was granted a charter in 1876 and was accorded city status in 1907.

The Handbook describes a town that kept its two halves separate on paper and joined in practice. Each side has its own mayor, council and city officials, while the two share fire service, food and dairy inspection, sewage disposal and some recreation programs. The Federal Building sits across the line and is called the only building of its kind situated in two states.

The same entry names the junction of Interstate 30 and U.S. highways 59, 67, 71 and 82, and ties the local economy to timber, farmland, minerals and railroads. It adds Texarkana College, three major hospitals, the Four States Fair and Rodeo, and Wright Patman Lake. Buyers who work at hospitals or the college, or who commute along I-30, are the natural audience for a Texarkana listing.

sections.h2: How many people does Texarkana, Texas have?
sections.html:
The city's own About Us page, which quotes a 2015 estimate, gives 37,280 people in the Texas city and a metro area spanning all of Bowie County and Miller County, Arkansas. It cites a combined 66,330 for the two cities at the 2010 census and 136,027 for the metropolitan area.

Those figures are older than most sellers would like, so treat them as scale, not as current counts. The takeaway: a Texarkana house competes for buyers across a small two-state metro, where employers on both sides pull workers to either city. Ask a Bowie County title company or the appraisal district for current local counts if you need them for a pricing conversation.

sections.h2: What can a Texarkana listing point to?
sections.html:
Local strengths come from the Handbook of Texas, which calls Texarkana the transportation, commercial and industrial center of the Texas-Arkansas area and a hub reaching into Oklahoma and Louisiana. It names crops such as cotton, corn, rice, soybeans and pecans, and industries from lumber to railroad tank cars and paper products.

  • Education and medicine: Texarkana College, which includes a nursing department, and three major hospitals.
  • Recreation: Wright Patman Lake, Millwood Reservoir across the line, and the annual Four States Fair and Rodeo.
  • Transportation: Interstate 30 and four U.S. highways meet here, and the entry calls the city a major Southwest rail center.

By 1896 the Handbook says the town already had waterworks, an electric light plant, streetcar lines, brick schools and a hotel, which hints at how old some of its neighborhoods may be. If your house is decades old, a buyer will want to see updates to wiring, plumbing and roofing, and records of those updates help.

sections.h2: What property tax dates does a Texarkana seller need?
sections.html:
Bowie Central Appraisal District follows the statewide schedule published by the Texas Comptroller, summarized here.

Property tax calendar as printed by the Comptroller
DateEvent
January 1Values set; tax lien attaches
April 30Many exemption applications due
May 15Usual protest deadline, or 30 days after the mailed notice, if later
October 1Bills mailed
January 31Final day before delinquency
February 1Delinquent; 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest begin

Bowie CAD's homepage links to a property tax calendar, a truth-in-taxation page on proposed rates, a payment portal and an exemption breakdown. For an exact payoff on your account, use the payment portal or ask the Bowie County tax office.

sections.h2: How do I protest a Bowie CAD appraisal?
sections.html:
The window runs to May 15 or to 30 days after the notice goes out, whichever lands later. Bowie CAD says owners whose market value rose by at least $1,000 receive a notice each spring listing market value, assessed value and taxable value.

  • By mail: P.O. Box 6527, Texarkana, TX 75505.
  • In person: 122A Plaza West in Texarkana or 710 James Bowie Drive in New Boston.
  • Online: through the portal, using the owner ID and PIN printed on the notice.

After filing, you can use an informal meeting with an appraiser, and Bowie CAD says informal meetings begin April 16 with one meeting per property. If you decline the settlement offer, the appraisal review board hears the case. Someone else may represent you if you complete an appointment of agent form.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and caps affect the price a buyer sees?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption lowers taxable value on a main residence, and the state caps homestead appraised value increases at 10 percent a year. Buyers who plan to live in the house will ask what the carrying cost looks like once their own exemption starts.

State rules give school districts a $140,000 homestead exemption, and senior and disabled owners get extra relief plus a school tax ceiling that can follow them to another Texas home. Disabled veterans have their own exemptions, scaled by rating. Apply through Bowie CAD, and ask how to end your own exemption after you sell.

sections.h2: What if I owe back taxes, inherited the house, or face foreclosure?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes come out of your sale money, and because the lien survives a change of owner, the title company will ask for a payoff. The Comptroller says some collectors allow plans of up to 36 months for homestead owners.

For an inherited house, heirs may go through probate, ask for a muniment of title, or rely on a deed that named a beneficiary and was recorded in the owner's lifetime. For foreclosure, the State Law Library says sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month with 21 days' notice. For squatters, Property Code chapter 24B allows a request to the sheriff or constable, but not against family members or current or former tenants. Talk to a Texas attorney about your case.

faqs.q: Is my Texarkana house governed by Texas or Arkansas law?
faqs.a: By the law of the state where it sits. A Texas-side house is in Bowie County and uses Texas rules. Check your deed and tax bill for the county.

faqs.q: When must I protest my Bowie CAD value?
faqs.a: By May 15, or 30 days after the notice is mailed if that is later. Informal meetings are offered first, then the appraisal review board.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texarkana house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, with penalty and interest, comes out of proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for a payoff good through your closing date.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair a house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers commonly take houses as is. A mortgage buyer is likelier to require repairs. Whether you list or sell for cash, gather receipts for any roof, plumbing or electrical work, since both kinds of buyer ask about the age of major systems and a clear paper trail speeds their decision.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Texas-side sale?
faqs.a: With the Bowie County Clerk, where the land is. Your title company normally handles the filing.
